root_idea.summary: The root centers on opening or releasing what is closed, bound, or restricted.
root_idea.development: From untying a knot, the root develops meanings of release and permissibility, alighting or settling after being bound for travel, reaching an appointed place, and becoming free of a sacred or legal restriction.

senses.definition: To untie, loosen, or release what is bound.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic imperative in the expression concerning the knot of the tongue preserves the concrete image of releasing a bond or impediment.

senses.definition: To alight, descend, settle, or come to rest in a place.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person, group, or thing arriving and settling; the form may be translated simply as descend or settle according to context.

senses.definition: Of anger, punishment, or a threatened consequence: to descend upon, befall, or become due.
senses.usage_conditions: This construction describes a consequence taking effect upon its object; it is distinct from merely settling in a place.

senses.definition: To become lawful, allowable, or free from a prohibition.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of something becoming permissible, including marital and other legal permissions.

senses.definition: To leave the state of ihram or another consecrated restriction.
senses.usage_conditions: In the pilgrimage context, the subject becomes free of the restrictions of ihram; this is a conventional extension of release from a bond.

senses.definition: To make lawful, permit, or declare free for use.
senses.usage_conditions: With protected or prohibited things, making lawful can imply treating what is sacred or restricted as permissible; passive forms mean that something has been made lawful.

senses.definition: To cause someone or something to alight, settle, or take up residence in a place.
senses.usage_conditions: The object is brought to or established in a place; in Quranic usage this includes bringing a people to a place and being settled in an abode.

senses.definition: A wife or spouse; حَلَائِل is its Quranic plural.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is plural and refers to the wives of sons.

senses.definition: Lawful, permitted, or allowable; the opposite of forbidden.
senses.usage_conditions: It describes food, provisions, or an act that religious or legal restriction does not prohibit.

senses.definition: Lawfulness or permissibility; a state in which something is not forbidden.
senses.usage_conditions: Used substantivally of food, persons, or relations that are legally permissible.

senses.definition: Freedom from consecrated restriction; the ordinary territory outside the sacred precinct.
senses.usage_conditions: The sense may describe a person who is not in ihram or a place outside the Haram; it is not merely a synonym for general moral freedom.

senses.definition: An appointed place or point at which something arrives or reaches its prescribed end, especially the lawful place of sacrifice.
senses.usage_conditions: In the pilgrimage passages it denotes the destination or appointed place where a sacrificial offering is to be slaughtered.

senses.definition: One who makes something lawful or treats it as permissible.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction with game and ihram, it denotes making the game permissible while the relevant consecrated restriction is in force.

senses.definition: The means by which an oath is released from its binding force, especially its expiation or kaffāra.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression, it refers to the prescribed act that dissolves the obligation of an oath.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dissolve, melt, or liquefy a solid or congealed thing.
To solve a problem or riddle, and by extension to analyze a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are figurative extensions of releasing something difficult or compounded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a sacrificial animal, to arrive at the place where it may lawfully be slaughtered.
To be free from an obligation or responsibility; of a woman, to become free of a marriage impediment; of an oath, to become discharged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are conventional release constructions distinct from the general adjective حلال.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical use recorded independently from the ordinary meanings of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man, to suffer pain in the hips or knees.
To do something only lightly or moderately, without exceeding the ordinary bounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage includes a slight blow, a restrained action, or a light contact with the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove or dispel a disease.
To clothe someone in a حُلَّة.
To cause punishment to befall someone or to make punishment become due upon him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a causative consequence construction, not the ordinary legal sense of permitting an act.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To release someone from an obligation, responsibility, or claim.
To enter the profane months, leave the sacred territory, or become free of an obligation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This intransitive or reflexive use is recorded in Classical Arabic outside the supplied Quran form evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make attack, fighting, or another prohibited act lawful against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe one who makes another's honour, property, or person open to attack.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a ewe, goat, or camel, to produce or release milk abundantly, sometimes without giving birth.
For an illness to go away gradually.
To finish one's prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use describing release from the state of prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a journey to leave a person ill, or for a person to fall ill after returning from a journey.
To become untied or undone; also to become dissolved, or for a problem to become solved and a thing analyzed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are intransitive or passive developments of releasing or loosening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relax or become free of self-restraint; of an oath, to become freed from its obligation.
To deem or account something lawful, or to ask that it be made lawful; hence, to profane or violate what should be protected.
To remove people from their place, unsettle them, and put them in motion.
A cry used to chide or urge a she-camel or camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cry is directed particularly to female camels in the cited lexical description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move away from a place, leave it, or become displaced.
Sesame oil or sesame seed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a homonymous nominal use distinguished by vocalization and lexical definition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A butt or other object used as a target for shooting or throwing.
A large basket or basket-shaped vessel, including a regional copper cooking pot.
The direction or intended course toward a thing.
Weakness or languor in a person.
A dress or suit of garments, especially one consisting of an izar and a ridaʾ or two matching garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word can also denote a fine or new garment in broader usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A weapon or set of weapons, figuratively something one puts on.
A wife, by metaphorical association with a garment or covering.
A mode or manner of alighting, lodging, or settling.
A settlement or collection of tents or houses, and by extension the people dwelling there.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote a large tribal encampment or a hundred or more houses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sitting place, assembly place, or the people gathered there.
Laxness or weakness in an animal's legs, hocks, tendons, or sinews.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description is especially associated with camels, though related animal usage is also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Paucity of flesh in the buttocks or thighs, or smallness and closeness of the buttocks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited description applies this term to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pain in a man's hips, haunches, or knees.
A man who has left ihram or is outside the sacred state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a substantivized person-description, distinct from the adjective meaning lawful.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman free of an impediment to marriage, such as having completed her waiting period.
A husband or fellow spouse; literally, one who shares a dwelling or intimate place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding feminine is حَلِيلَة; the Quranic plural حَلَائِل refers to wives.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fellow-lodger or fellow-resident in one house.
A neighbour.
A guest.
One who solves astronomical problems.
Blood that goes for nothing or is treated as having no account.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This occurs in the cited idiom about blood being unavenged.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grave, steadfast, courageous, or prominent chief; a man of weight and virtue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical restriction applies the term to a man, not a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who unties, undoes, or opens a knot; the act of untying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the active-participial noun of the concrete untying construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who alights, settles, lodges, or abides in a place; also a settled or alighting group.
A person who completes recitation of the Quran and immediately begins it again.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic designation based on the image of one who is continually travelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Due or falling due; the end of the appointed term of a debt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun مَحِلّ can denote the time or term when payment becomes due.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the laxness or weakness called حَلَل in the legs or hocks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited usage is chiefly applied to horses, camels, and similar animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a woman, having little flesh in the buttocks or thighs.
The orifice through which urine passes from the penis, or milk passes from the breast or udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an anatomical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where a person or group alights, lodges, settles, or takes up residence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote a particular settlement-place or place of arrival.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in a general sense, including a position or syntactic place occupied by something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This includes the grammatical expression for a word's syntactic position.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grammatical term for an adverbial noun of place or time.
A person regarded as a suitable locus or instance for a quality to be predicated of him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a figurative extension of place or locus.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The term or appointed time when a debt falls due.
One who makes a person alight or settle; also, in a specialized usage, the equipment that enables a traveller to settle wherever he wishes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The equipment is enumerated as cooking, milling, cutting, lighting, water, and related camp implements.

other_classical_meanings.definition: That which makes a debt fall due or brings its appointed term near.
A person against whom fighting or killing is regarded as lawful, or who has no protected covenant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the contralateral legal sense to مُحْرِم in the cited descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who violates something sacred or does not recognize the sanctity of a sacred month.
Water at which camels have stayed and consequently made turbid.
A man whose remarriage to a wife divorced three times has become lawful after her intervening marriage and divorce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized legal-marital term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing small in quantity.
A man who marries a thrice-divorced woman with the arrangement that he will divorce her after consummation so that she may remarry her former husband.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the specialized legal-marital use of the active participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a race for stakes, the third participant who enters without staking and thereby makes the contest lawful under the described rules.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: If he wins he takes the stakes; if he loses he is not fined.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place, meadow, land, or house where people frequently alight or settle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also imply a place that invites or supports frequent settlement, especially through abundant herbage.

cautions: The Quranic Form I verb has distinct vocalized and constructional uses: untying, settling or descending, becoming due, becoming lawful, and leaving ihram should not be collapsed into one gloss.
The public headword حَلِيلَة is normalized from the Quranic plural حَلَائِل; the supplied occurrence itself is plural.
The public headword مُحِلّ is normalized from the Quranic active-participial form مُحِلِّى.
Lane's Quran references in its primary text were not converted into modern verse locations unless the corresponding QAC location was supplied and secure.
